## In one sentence

Estimation uses data to learn about an unknown population quantity and reports
both an estimate and its uncertainty.

## Estimates and standard errors

An estimator is a rule that maps a sample to a value. Its standard error measures
how much that estimator would vary across repeated samples under a model. More
data often reduces standard error, but systematic bias is not fixed by sample
size alone.

A simple approximate interval is:

$$
\text{estimate} \pm \text{critical value} \times \text{standard error}
$$

The critical value depends on the reference distribution and the desired
coverage.

## Interpreting confidence intervals

A 95% confidence procedure produces intervals that contain the fixed parameter
in about 95% of repeated samples when its assumptions hold. It does not mean
there is a 95% probability that this one fixed parameter lies in this interval.

::: {.callout-tip}
Interpret the interval in the units of the outcome and compare its width with
effects that would matter in practice.
:::

## Check your understanding

Explain what would make an interval wider: a smaller sample, greater outcome
variability, or a higher confidence level.
